findings.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:11 unconditionally indexes category query row [0], causing migration failure before the fallback when embed_category is unset or references a deleted category and blocking upgrades.

db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 inserts existing hosts without stripping URL schemes, causing values such as https://example.com to fail uri.host comparisons and breaking existing embeds.
app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2 limits top-level domains to five letters, preventing valid hosts such as example.museum and example.technology from being added or saved.
app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17 accepts hosts containing ports, but lookup compares them against uri.host without the port, so saved hosts such as example.com:8080 never authorize embeds.

goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2 limits top-level domains to five letters, preventing valid hosts such as example.museum and example.technology from being added or saved.

adjudication.rationale: The finding points to line 2 of app/models/embeddable_host.rb which contains the regex validation: `validates_format_of :host, :with => /\A[a-z0-9]+([\-\.]{1}[a-z0-9]+)*\.[a-z]{2,5}(:[0-9]{1,5})?(\/.*)?\Z/i`. The regex pattern `[a-z]{2,5}` at the end limits the top-level domain to 2-5 characters. This would indeed reject valid TLDs like '.museum' (6 chars), '.technology' (10 chars), and many other newer gTLDs that exceed 5 characters. This is a real correctness bug that would prevent legitimate hosts from being saved.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17 accepts hosts containing ports, but lookup compares them against uri.host without the port, so saved hosts such as example.com:8080 never authorize embeds.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the EmbeddableHost model, the validation regex on line 2 allows hosts with ports: `/\A[a-z0-9]+([\-\.]{1}[a-z0-9]+)*\.[a-z]{2,5}(:[0-9]{1,5})?(\/.*)?\/i`. However, the before_validation hook on lines 5-8 strips the protocol and path but NOT the port. In the record_for_host method (lines 10-18), it extracts `uri.host` which in Ruby's URI library returns just the hostname without the port. So if someone saves 'example.com:8080' as a host, the lookup does `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` where host is just 'example.com' (without port), but the stored value is 'example.com:8080'. This is a real mismatch that would cause authorization to fail for hosts with ports.
